To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the depletion of intracellulat Ca2+ stores stimulates Ca2+ influx into pancreatic β‐cells by two mechanisms, a capacitative Ca2+, entry and a potentiation of the voltage‐dependent Ca+2 entry, and that these two mechanisms may act in concert to amplify the glucose‐induced oscillations of [Ca2+], which are believed to be the trigger of insulin secretion.

the depletion of intracelular stores of Ca2+ in mouse pancreatic beta‐cells stimulates the entry of Ca2+ into the cell by two different mechanisms: a capacitative Ca2+-entry, which is small, and a potentiation of voltage‐dependent calcium channels, which is large.

(1) in pancreatic β‐cells, the emptying intracellular stores by thapsagin induces a small capacitive Ca2+ influx, but (2) the main effect of thapsagin on [Ca2+]I oscillations is due to a potentiation of voltage‐dependent, glucose‐induced, Ca2+ entry.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the mechanisms by which Ca2+ influx is regulated in pancreatic β‐cells, which are specialized endocrine cells responsible for the synthesis and secretion of insulin.
the role of intracellular calcium stores in the control of calcium entry into pancreatic β‐cells, and in their function as glucose‐sensitive cells.
the mechanisms of Ca2+ signalling and the regulation of Ca2+ homeostasis in pancreatic β‐cells, which are responsible for insulin secretion.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the emptying of Ca2+ stores by thapsgargin in β‐cells causes a small capacitative entry, a depolarization, and a potentiation of the Ca2+ influx.

in pancreatic β‐cells, the emptying intracellular stores by the inhibitor of the sarco‐endoplasmic reticulum Ca2+‐ATPase, thapsigargin, stimulates Ca2+ entry through both direct and indirect (i.e., through the potentiation of voltage‐dependent calcium channels) mechanisms.
the emptying of the intracellular Ca2 stores in pancreatic β‐cells induces both a capacitative Ca entry and an indirect effect on voltage‐dependent Ca entry.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
Ca2+ influx is regulated in pancreatic β‐cells by two distinct mechanisms, namely the activation of Ca2+ channels and capacitative Ca2+.
the emptying of Ca2+ stores stimulates Ca2+ entry by both direct and indirect mechanisms.
thapsigargin‐induced Ca(2+)-influx is a result of a combination of both direct and indirect mechanisms in pancreatic β‐cells.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the emptying of Ca2+ stores by thapsigrain (TG) in pancreatic islets causes a transient increase in [Ca2+], which is not due to capacitative Ca2+.
the emptying of Ca2+ stores stimulates Ca2+ entry by a direct and an indirect mechanism in β‐cells.
the emptying of Ca2+ stores is not only a mechanism to maintain the Ca2+ concentration in the cell but also a way to increase the influx of Ca2+ through voltage‐dependent channels.
